subject: PO onboarding: acceptance window, invoice-phase gating & payment-lane alignment
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@scalehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Purchase order requirements and invoice cadence question

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're preparing the PO and need to align on a few procurement items before I route to finance:

- Net terms: our standard is Net 60. Is Redwood able to accept Net 60? If not, what conditions (prepayment, credit holdback) would change that?
- PO fields: we need an acceptance window and an explicit invoice-phase field to map into our ERP. Can you provide a template that includes the acceptance timeline (e.g., 10 business days) and a PO number mapping?
- Invoice cadence: our default is monthly, but for this scope we'd prefer quarterly tranche invoices (one invoice per quarter) with a 3% holdback until acceptance of each tranche. Will Redwood accept quarterly invoices or do you require monthly billing?

I've attached a sample PO and our vendor onboarding checklist for reference.

Attachment: PO_1234.pdf (pdf)

Please confirm what works and any internal approvals needed.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Procurement Lead, ScaleHealth
procurement@scalehealth.com

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Procurement Team <procurement@scalehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase order requirements and invoice cadence question

Anna —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear checklist. Quick answers up front:

- Net terms: Redwood typically invoices Net 30. We can accommodate Net 60 for enterprise customers under a signed commitment (deal RDW-7452) if we have either (a) a quarterly advance payment covering the first quarter, or (b) a 3% holdback applied to each invoice until acceptance is confirmed.
- PO fields & acceptance window: we can populate the PO with an explicit "Acceptance Window" field. Our standard acceptance window is 10 business days after invoice submission; we can shorten to 5 business days for prioritized onboarding. I'll attach a PO acceptance matrix that maps the PO fields to our ERP codes.
- Invoice cadence: Redwood supports monthly, quarterly, and milestone invoicing. Quarterly tranche invoices are fine, but billing alignment affects cycle start/renewal dates and support of usage reconciliation. To accept quarterly invoices with a 3% holdback we need the PO to include: (i) invoice-phase (Q1/Q2/etc), (ii) acceptance criteria for each tranche, and (iii) a billing contact for reconciliation.

I've attached our SAAS order form and a PO_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.xlsx to help the mapping. If you can share the exact ERP field names (vendor code / GL / cost center) we'll prefill the order form before you route it.

Next steps:
1) If Net 60 is required, confirm whether ScaleHealth will accept the 3% holdback model or a Q1 advance.
2) Share ERP field names + preferred invoice cadence (quarterly preferred option noted).
3) Once we have that, Vanessa will produce a prefilled order form and I will route to finance for the Net 60 exception approval.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_SAAS_ORDER_FORM_v1.pdf (pdf); PO_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.xlsx (xlsx)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, Procurement Team <procurement@scalehealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-02T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Purchase order requirements and invoice cadence question

Hi Anna / Ben —

Looping in accounting notes so everything's explicit on the PO:

- Acceptance gating: our ops prefers a 10-business-day acceptance window by default. For quarterly tranches we can tag each tranche with an "acceptance flag" that triggers release of the 3% holdback. We will record acceptance timestamps in our audit log for your finance team.
- Billing mapping: please provide the vendor code + GL + cost center. If you cannot provide cost center per tranche we will bill to the master cost center and include PO line-level metadata to help your ERP match.
- Net terms exception flow: for Net 60 we require a written approval from Redwood Finance (I can request the exception; turnaround 48-72 hours with deal docs in HubSpot). Alternatively, a Q1 advance prefund removes the need for an exception.

Operationally we prefer the following to speed onboarding:
1) ScaleHealth confirms monthly vs quarterly (we recommend quarterly if you're consolidating reporting).
2) Procurement returns the completed PO template with ERP fields populated.
3) Ben tags the HubSpot deal RDW-7452 with "PO-ready" and I file a Net 60 exception request if needed.

I'll prepare the prefilled order form once we get the ERP fields; Grace, can you confirm whether we have any existing credit terms with ScaleHealth on record?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
